validator: draft 1 passed with no hard or soft problems; the faults below are the critic's
keep: The idea is named up front in plain words: a force turns as well as pushes, and its turning effect is force times the distance at right angles to its line, recalled from the Vectors spanner (150 N on 0.3 m, 45 N m) rather than re-taught.
The rule is stated in words and worked with real numbers on the brief's beam: 6 kN at 1 m on a 4 m span gives 1.5 kN and 4.5 kN, then the up forces add to the load, tying back to Forces in balance.

Thirteen screens alternate SHOW (1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11) and DO (2, 4, 6, 8, 10), ending with two mixed puzzles (12, 13). Each brief misconception has its own wrong pick: the slanted bar's length used as the arm (2, wrong 100 N m), the far support taking more because more beam is on its side (6), the beam's own weight left out or put off its middle (10, wrong 1 kN and 4 kN; 13, wrong 3 kN and 5 kN).

The analogy is from Dan's trade and reproduces the main result exactly: a point load splits between two supports in inverse proportion to their distances, as a current splits between two parallel resistances. Its break, the overhang, is true and is a safety point.
Six footnotes, at most one a sentence, on the rule and the unit he would look up; no source named in the words.
fix: False absolute: 'The nearer trestle always carries more' sits next to the equal share at the middle. Drop 'always'.

Causal step skipped: 'Only the right-angle distance counts, because a force can slide along its own line' leaves him to see why that picks the right-angle distance. Add the step: slide the force along its line to the point nearest the pivot; there the distance meets the line at right angles.
Causal step skipped: 'Something that stays still does not start to turn' gives no reason. Say any leftover turning effect would start it turning, as a leftover force would start it moving.
Causal step skipped: 'the right trestle carries 10 ÷ 4' with beam weight; the 10 appears from nowhere. Show 6 + 4 = 10 kN m.
The uniform beam's weight 'since it is the same either side' is thin. Say each half of the beam balances the other about the middle, so the whole weight acts as one force there.

Talks about instead of teaching: 'One more case only turns' and 'which comes back with rotation' are vague. Teach the couple with the valve wheel's numbers (100 N each side of a 0.4 m wheel: 40 N m about the centre and about either hand) and say plainly that a motor's twist on its shaft is one.
The interactive could show the cause more plainly: mark each trestle's arm, its distance from the block, on the beam, so he sees the far trestle's longer arm while its arrow shrinks.
Interactive: the spread load 'centred where the block was' runs off the beam near either end. Keep its centre between 1 m and 3 m, so it always lies on the beam.
Unreadable label: the readout 'Each way about the pivot' does not say what it is. Call it 'Moment each way'.
Practice rule of thumb: 'its distance to the other support' is ambiguous. Say the load's distance from the other support.
No recall checks (taught mode, checks empty).
